name: KY-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+32 partisan lean makes a Democratic win structurally improbable
Hal Rogers is a decades-entrenched incumbent with a large money advantage ($850K raised vs. $182K)
Prediction markets price Rogers near 97% to win
No polls or expert ratings exist, but no evidence of a competitive race has emerged
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Rogers: an R+32 district, a long-tenured incumbent, and a fundraising edge of more than four-to-one over Ned Pillersdorf, with prediction markets pricing the Democrat at just 4%. With no polls or ratings suggesting competition, the forecast stays firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing a single-digit race, a major scandal or health issue for Rogers, or significant outside spending against him would be the first signs of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kentucky's 5th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and Hal Rogers has held it for decades. He is running again with a substantial financial advantage, having raised roughly $850,000 to Democrat Ned Pillersdorf's $182,000, and he enters the general election with far more cash on hand. Two independent candidates trail with negligible funding.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on the district's R+32 lean, Rogers's incumbency, and his fundraising edge. Prediction markets give Rogers about a 97% chance of winning. Absent unexpected developments, this race is not considered competitive, and Pillersdorf would need an extraordinary shift in the political environment to threaten the seat.
